transcript.text: I understand your fridge-freezer isn't getting cold. This is often caused by restricted airflow rather than a major mechanical failure. The most common reason for this is simply that the vents (usually on the back wall of the fridge section) are blocked by food or over-packing, which stops the cold air from circulating properly. Another possibility is that the defrost drain at the bottom of the fridge compartment has become blocked with ice or debris. First, please check if any items are pressed against those vents inside the fridge. If they are, move them aside to ensure there is a clear gap for air to flow. Let me know if you find this was the case.
moved food away from the back, no difference. freezer still freezing fine, just the fridge warm

Since moving the food didn't help, we are looking at airflow again. In most fridge-freezers, cold air is made in the freezer and pushed into the fridge by a fan or gravity through vents. If that path is blocked by ice, the freezer stays cold but the fridge goes warm. The two main possibilities now are:
1. The defrost system has failed, causing a block of ice to form over the cooling coils (choking the airflow).
2. The evaporator fan motor has stopped working (so no air is being pushed into the fridge). To tell them apart, please do this check:
1. Open the freezer door and look at the back wall. Is there a thick block of ice or heavy frost covering the coils?
2. With the door shut (you may need to press the light switch in with your finger), listen carefully for a faint whirring sound from inside. Let me know what you see regarding the ice, and whether you hear the fan.
yes thick white frost on the back wall, more than ive ever seen. can hear a faint scraping/ticking from the freezer sometimes. no burning smell or tripping

That thick frost on the back wall suggests the issue: your fridge-freezer has a defrost fault. The system that normally melts ice off the coils has failed, so a solid block of ice has formed over the evaporator coil. This blocks the airflow into the fridge section, which is why the freezer stays cold but the fridge goes warm. The faint scraping or ticking you hear is likely the fan motor trying to spin against the ice or hitting it. To confirm this and restore cooling temporarily, we need to clear the blockage manually:
1. Switch the appliance off at the wall socket.
2. Remove all food and place it in cool bags with ice packs (or a neighbour's freezer) to keep it cold.
3. Lay towels inside both compartments to catch the water.
4. Leave both doors wide open for 24 hours until every bit of ice has melted.
5. Dry everything thoroughly, then plug it back in and set it to normal settings. Please let me know if the cooling returns after this full defrost. If it does but the frost builds up again within a few days, we will need to replace one of the defrost components (usually the heater or thermostat).
did the full defrost. fridge got cold again within a day, 3C. but after about 5 days its starting to creep up again

The fact that cooling returns for a few days but then fails again as the frost builds up suggests this is an automatic defrost fault. The system that melts the ice isn't working, so the blockage keeps returning. There are two likely parts at fault:
1. The defrost heater (the element that melts the ice) has burned out.
2. The defrost thermostat or thermal fuse (which tells the heater when to turn on) has failed and is stuck 'off'. Before we look at replacing these, please check one simple thing: once the ice has melted, look for a small drain hole at the bottom of that back wall in the freezer. If this gets blocked with slush or ice, water can't escape and refreezes into a blockage even if the heater is working. Was the drain hole blocked when you cleared it, or was it clear?
not sure, didn't see the drain hole. how do I find it?

The drain is usually located at the very bottom of the back wall inside the freezer compartment (sometimes hidden under a small plastic cover). Once you have cleared all the ice from your full defrost, look for a small hole or channel there. If you see water sitting in there or slush blocking it, please clear it gently with warm water using a turkey baster or soft pipe cleaner. Was this drain hole blocked when you looked at it after defrosting?
didn't see it when I defrosted so don't know if it was blocked. is it behind the back panel? I can't take that off

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, on most models that drain hole is behind a small plastic cover or panel inside the freezer. Since you cannot remove that panel yourself, we can skip checking it directly. The pattern of symptoms—thick frost building up again after a few days despite a full manual defrost—suggests this is an automatic defect in the defrost system. The part responsible for melting that ice (usually the heater element or the thermostat controlling it) has likely failed and needs replacing. Because accessing these parts requires removing the internal back panel, this is not a safe job to attempt without experience. I recommend calling out a qualified engineer to replace the faulty defrost component. In the meantime, you can keep using the appliance by performing a manual defrost every time the fridge temperature starts to rise (usually every 3–5 days), but be aware that this will not fix the underlying fault.
